newsitem.title: POLAND: Pekao initiates Optimus with "buy" rate. [CORRECTED 12:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Pekao initiates Optimus with "buy" rate. [CORRECTED 12:30 GMT]

text.p: The shares of Polish computer maker Optimus SA are underpriced and are worth buying, the brokerage unit of Bank Pekao SA said in a report.

It said Optimus was well-placed to take advantage of the growing computer market in Poland and should enjoy significant growth in sales and profits from core activities in 1996 and 1997, the report dated November 13 said.
On that day Optimus closed at 38.8 zlotys on the Warsaw bourse and has since risen to 42.5 zlotys.
Pekao said Optimus's multimedia, integration and telecommunication activities would help keep margins high over the next few years and that the firm's management and financial costs should decrease.
It said the firm's convertible bonds would likely be converted over the next two years and allow Optimus to achieve its desired investment.
The firm's $30 million (Corrects from $30 billion) international convertible bond issue of 300 five-year bonds are exchangeable into 6,947 common shares at 38.76 zlotys a share.
Optimus has made a net profit of 10 million zlotys over the first 10 months this year against 9.2 million zlotys for all of last year.
In October it said it would earn 17.5 million zlotys this year and increase group net to 21 million zlotys from last year's 12.2 million zlotys.
